tasks.title: Init and day-2 commands share cli/lock.ts identities, durable writes and fenced API transport
tasks.spec: ## Repository: deploy, Reuse (extract before the second use), shared files and Tool facts; Decisions 3-4, 7-9 and 13; Acceptance evidence 3 (Lock and shared test seams), Security impact and Rollout order. FIRST extract the lock and atomicWrite/link/mode checks from cli/write-install.ts into cli/lock.ts and cli/safe-write.ts, with their tests, and migrate init. Preserve ownership-by-content release and recorded signals. Extend lock with Decision 3's five-line pid/nonce/host/started/command content and environment-independent process identity behind injected process.kill/platform/hostname/three-/proc-read/files seams. Never run ps, spawn a process or format a time. Linux identity is linux:<boot_id>:<pid-namespace-inode>:<field22-starttime-ticks>; Export ONE pure startTicks(statText) parser in cli/lock.ts: text after the last ')', split on single spaces, index19 for field22, validated 1-20 decimal digits. Support command names with spaces/parentheses. Both lock identity and API_SCRIPT use this parser; the latter embeds String(startTicks), never a second implementation. Invalid/unreadable identity is '-'; macOS uses '-' without reading /proc. Implement every stale-judgement table row: same host/boot/namespace permits ESRCH or a running pid with valid different ticks; same boot/different namespace never breaks; different boot breaks; mixed Linux/'-' never breaks; '-'/ '-' breaks only ESRCH. EPERM/unreadable live stat/doubt refuse. Break under wx 0600 .pulse-init.lock.break, byte-equal reread, unlink/own wx/directory fsync; refuse foreign-host, legacy, live, invalid and changing locks and always release an owned break file. Acquire before guard/journal/upgrade.json/recovery reads. Rewrite docs/cli.md's stale-lock guidance for init, token rotate and upgrade, including the Linux/macOS identity rules, shared-host/manual checks and both lock files; explain unsupported shared directories on distinct machines with one hostname. Add matching docs assertions now. Environment fixtures and real-/proc Linux child-process tests belong here; T6 captures Linux identity output and the explicit non-Linux skip (no ps evidence). safe-write.ts owns the single validated-state reader/durable writer, safe writes and archive finalization with file and directory fsync. One injected file seam exposes mkdir/open/read/write/file-fsync/rename/directory-fsync/unlink and records creates, token-file lstat/reads and all persistence events in the same ordered log as fake Docker. It supports T5's power-loss view: only parent-fsynced entries and file-fsynced content survive; T5 owns the crash-prefix checks and broken variants. It must preserve observable on-disk renames when a later fsync throws, offer ONE validated read-back after a failed state write without retry, and simulate errors or hard kills without cleanup. Consumer reconciliation/action tables stay in T4/T5. Extend cli/docker.ts's sole spawn for input/stdinFd/stdoutFd, default ignored stdin, fd bytes and binary-named ENOENT (Docker remains exit 3, gh becomes exit 1). Return checkConfig's already-parsed effective Compose model in Project, with own()/isObj readers; preserve override/--no-interpolate and one resolution call. FIRST extract checkVolumes' existing inspect-and-two-label comparison into one exported cli/docker.ts function with tests returning missing, owned, foreign or inspect error. Keep the guard skipping missing volumes and rejecting foreign ones; T5 consumes this function to REQUIRE existing owned snapshot volumes before mutation and around helpers, without duplicating label checks. Reuse INSTALL_LABEL from cli/render-compose.ts. Export and reuse PULSE_IMAGE/assertPin from cli/services.ts with runtime-assembled shape fixtures. Extend parsePs for full ID and readyz/waitReady for container targeting; no duplicate guard, poller, pin pattern or spawn. cli/api-call.ts owns constant API_SCRIPT (stdin JSON, fixed localhost URL, 10 s fetch, 11 s unref'd exit 70, redirect:error, 1 MiB cap). Extend it with Decision 4 Instance fence: compute <boot_id>:<startTicks(/proc/1/stat)> inside the api container, or '-' on read/shape failure; print instance <value> on line1, status on line2, then body. GET ignores stdin instance/null. EVERY rotate/create/revoke POST requires a non-'-' instance equal to the script's current one; mismatch/null/missing/'-' prints fenced on line2 and exits71 BEFORE ANY network connection. All instance values and bearers travel on stdin, never argv/env; the calling seam returns the parsed instance for the next write. No first POST is possible with unreadable instance; use the spec's recovery hint. Implement Acceptance 3 API script against the REAL script/local listener on Linux: independent cat/awk instance, literal mismatch and missing/null/'-' writes ->71/0 connections; matching write and GET ->1 connection each, with printed skip reasons outside Linux or on occupied port/unsupported PID1 name. No Docker or gh requirement for these local tests. It also owns and the timingSafeEqual file-comparison script (stdin expected secret, same/different only, 10 s bound). The client ending is never a server barrier: implement no settle process scan or SETTLE_SCRIPT. Extend cli/test/fake-docker.ts as the sole fake spawn with input/fds/signals/full ids/states/labels and named stop-at-step hooks. Prepare API stop/start/inspect with a distinct instance on every start; model pending compose exec clients separately from the daemon as well as pending helpers. Delivering an exec executes the script's real fence decision in the CURRENT api instance; a stale POST has no network/API request. T4 owns delivery-at-every-later-event and unchanged/unreadable-instance barrier matrices. Prepare per-volume inspect answers, -v creating a missing volume WITHOUT labels, and helpers surviving client death for T4/T5. Model Docker client and daemon separately with pending create/start/run requests deliverable after a killed run, inert created containers, rm -f ending all phases, and start of a removed id failing No such container; T5 owns the shared two-step launcher, pending-client and helper-phase matrices. T4 owns server-write fault matrices. Each shared module states its ownership and tests its variants.

Reject every other mount at/below/above a writable volume (including /), while allowing harmless tmpfs/config/secret elsewhere. Around snapshot/abort failure: sweep helpers, keep snapshotting/all archives, no aborted/deletion/start/further helper. Around restore failure: sweep then rollback-failed/restored:false, no start. Require installed authenticated gh; verify each changed digest within 120 s with repo/signer-workflow/source-ref/deny-self-hosted-runners even in preview, no bypass/re-resolution; pull/write that exact digest. Immediately after guard sweep leftover helpers by existing INSTALL_LABEL+new helper label BEFORE nonterminal-directory refusal, then reject journal/incomplete/unreadable snapshot metadata. Helper sweep: list by both labels, rm -f each full id, list empty; <=3 rounds/30 s, print count when nonzero; failure names ids/recovery link with no state/restore/start. Never rely on Compose down or client kill to end standalone helpers. Label every snapshot/restore helper; use only resolved pinned secrets-init image and Decision 13 restricted network/capabilities. FIRST implement ONE shared helper launcher in cli/snapshot.ts for snapshot and restore: docker create --rm with labels/options and stdin -i only for restore, 30 s bound; require exit0 and exactly one 64-lowerhex id line; ONLY its same live invocation may spawn docker start -a <id> (snapshot stdout fd) or docker start -a -i <id> (restore stdin fd). No production helper docker run and no starting ids found by a sweep. Check volume BEFORE CREATE (create already mounts it), and after start exits. Invalid id/create/start failure triggers sweep and the step's failure path. Model pending client requests separately from containers: late create leaves inert created helper; late start before rm is killed by rm, late start after rm fails No such container; sweeps include --all. A killed-create client cannot cause a later helper phase; tests must prove one-step run variant violates this. A pending create may leave an inert container after an empty sweep and refusal; next sweep removes it. Do not infer daemon completion from client death. Sweep during abort, before first restore, after nonzero/throwing restore spawn before state write, and before EVERY upgrade/abort/rollback up. Before stopping anything, durably create the snapshot directory CHAIN in Decision 13 step4 order: mkdir .pulse-upgrade 0700 when absent, fsync install directory EVEN WHEN .pulse-upgrade already exists, mkdir unique snapshot 0700, fsync .pulse-upgrade, then four-part snapshotting write/fsync snapshot directory. Failure cleans only newly created snapshot contents/directory, keeps pre-existing .pulse-upgrade, exits1/could not create the snapshot directory with 0 stops/helpers; cleanup failure leaves a blocking directory. Snapshot streams each sorted existing owned volume to wx0600 .tar.part, fsync/size/hash/rename/directory fsync; copy Compose with wx0600/file-fsync/snapshot-directory-fsync and verify composeSha256. T5 uses the shared file/fake-spawn log for directory-chain failures and simulated power-loss prefixes, and proves detection with variants omitting each required parent fsync. States snapshotting/applying/done/aborted/rolling-back/restored/rolled-back/rollback-failed with restored boolean and validated external input. Complete boundary is on-disk applying+tars, but only durable applying permits switch. State-write failures use ONE validated disk read-back and Decision 13 table, no write retry: snapshotting cleanup before stop; applying readback snapshotting aborts, applying+tars rolls back, invalid/unreadable/unexpected stops with no delete/restore/start. Abort only from disk snapshotting: sweep, unchanged Compose hash, passing volume checks for every snapshotVolumes entry, aborted, delete archives only after durable aborted; failed aborted keeps archives but starts unchanged old stack. Rollback: durable rolling-back, stop, verify ALL tars and Compose before any data change, helper sweep, restore every volume with exact script find /to -mindepth 1 -delete && tar -C /to -xpf - && sync -f /to, restore Compose durably, durable restored, sweep/up/readiness. Each helper must exit 0 INCLUDING sync before restored; failed helper sync/extraction/spawn or Compose restore leads to sweep then rollback-failed/restored:false/no up. Failed rolling-back/restored state writes stop with no subsequent restore/start. Ready rollback -> rolled-back; failed old readiness -> rollback-failed/restored:true. Failed terminal writes preserve final stack shape with warning/exit 1; never turn failed done into rollback. Edit only image strings with count/model check and mode preserved. Record signals through state-error resolution and rollback; outputs/timeouts/0/1/130 per spec. Fake helpers keep running after client/CLI death, record delete/extract/sync phases and stop only at rm -f. Pending-client tests deliver create/start after either sweep list, refusal or manual-recovery start, for both helper kinds; created helpers execute 0 phases and removed ids never run. Include 30 s create-timeout failure path and mutation test with one-step docker run. Every hard-kill case keeps lock, rerun breaks it then sweeps BEFORE refusing nonterminal directory; no automatic upgrade resume. Wire HELP/COMMANDS/dispatch/errors and command docs/manual equivalents. Upgrade recovery ALWAYS starts with waiting for surviving Docker clients of the project via Decision 13's pgrep command (pending compose up can otherwise race the restore), THEN helper removal by BOTH labels/list empty including created helpers BEFORE pulse down/restore/up; never docker start a helper. Manual foreground restore may use the specified labelled docker run with sync, unlike the production launcher; per-state facts-on-disk recovery, tar hashes, sync -f /to, restored true/false, stale lock, existing owned named-volume/default-path requirements (run pulse up once first), bind-to-volume migration, refusal if volumes disappear and backup recovery for helper-created unlabelled volumes, durable directory chain before stop, downtime/lost writes/disk space and Linux syncfs writeback-error kernel limit. Doc tests check pgrep THEN helper label before first recovery pulse down, no docker start command, sync in restore and all 3 lock-holder commands. Real hard-kill/manual restore proof belongs to T6.
